newsitem.title: USA: Ill. tollway says will appeal court budget ruling.
newsitem.headline: Ill. tollway says will appeal court budget ruling.

text.p: The Illinois State Toll Highway Authority will appeal a state judge's decision last week overturning a decades old budget practice, a spokesman said Monday.
"Obviously we believe we have been operating within the constitution and the statutes of the state," Tollway spokesman David Loveday said.

A Cook County judge Wednesday held that language in the tollway law allowing the authority to make continuing appropriations without submitting a budget to the governor or General Assembly violates the Illinois Constitution.

State law permits continuing appropriations carefully limited to the service and repayment of a multi-year finite debt, but the language in the act gives the authority "the unfettered power to spend whatever it collects, for whatever it chooses," Judge Stephen Schiller wrote.
Schiller's ruling came as part of a taxpayer lawsuit filed in 1995 that seeks an accounting of the authority's use of tolls to expand the system.

"This unconstitutional practice by the Illinois State Toll Highway Authority has led, over the past years, to numerous abuses in spending and has put the state in a spending program involving hundreds of millions of dollars without accountability of any kind," a lawyer for the plaintiffs, Mike Cherry of Chicago, said in a statement.
Loveday said the Tollway will ask the Illinois Supreme Court to review the decision and noted that the authority has been operating under the same budget system for four decades.
"The way the statute is set up, we collect the toll revenues and we have a board that approves the budget," Loveday said. "That is what the board is here for."
